items.title: Labour Day Toronto and Ontario cities: What’s Open and Closed
items.summary: This year, Labour Day falls on Sept. 7, 2026, in Mississauga, Brampton, Toronto, Hamilton, Oakville, Milton, Burlington, Oshawa, Whitby, Pickering, Clarington, Niagara Falls and the Niagara Region. While government buildings, services and many businesses/stores will be closed on Monday, some places will remain open. However, to avoid disappointment, it’s best to call ahead or check online to confirm if your favourite restaurant or local grocery store is open. Here’s what’s open and closed in southern Ontario towns and cities on Labour Day: Square One Shopping Centre is open, along with Walmart Supercentre, The Rec Room and The Food District. Whole Foods Square One and T&T Supermarket are also open. Residents and visitors can also visit Celebration Square and the Celebration Square fountain, Rabba grocery stores, select Beer Store locations, the YMCA health and fitness centre in Mississauga, restaurants, cafes, and bars that are typically open on Mondays (call ahead to confirm), the Mississauga Chinese Centre, and movie theatres. On Sept. 7, non-emergency federal, provincial, municipal (including City Hall), and Region of Peel offices will be closed. Banks, libraries and some community centres will also be closed. Canada Post will be closed (no mail pickup or delivery), and there will be no waste collection on Labour Day. Garbage and recycling will be picked up one day later than usual, and Community Recycling Centres will also be closed. items.title: Suspect still on the loose after stabbing leaves victim critical in Mississauga
items.summary: A person is fighting for their life in hospital following a stabbing in Mississauga that led to a large police presence and a search for a suspect. m. following reports of a stabbing. Police said one person was found suffering from critical injuries and was transported to a trauma centre. One suspect was taken into custody following the incident, while officers searched the surrounding area for a second suspect. In an update, police said the stabbing was believed to be an isolated incident and there was no ongoing threat to public safety. The outstanding suspect is described by police as a Hispanic woman in her mid-30s, approximately five-foot-four, with blonde and brown hair. The victim remained in critical condition at a trauma centre as of the latest police update. Officers remained in the Main Street and Dundas Street East area as the investigation continued.

items.title: Mississauga aims to secure over $401M in funding for housing support infrastructure
items.summary: Ontario students can expect a mix of sun and cloud on Tuesda… City staff are backing the proposal for the 3-acre Dixie sit… If approved, the funding will support two transit projects including a new Transit Mobility Hub. 4 million from the provincial and federal governments, with that money going toward housing and transit infrastructure. 4 million from the federal and provincial governments to support housing and transit infrastructure, officials announced on Sept. 3. The funding comes through the Development Charges Reduction Program, part of the Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. The initiative supports municipalities that have reduced development charges to spur housing development, according to a city news release. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Premier Doug Ford and other government officials made the announcement. Mississauga secured the funds after becoming one of the first Ontario cities to cut development charges by 100 per cent for certain types of housing developments to encourage growth. This reduction remains in effect until March 31, 2029.

items.summary: City staff are backing the proposal for the 3-acre Dixie site — Mississauga’s planning committee votes Sept. 8. Two 16-storey apartment buildings connected by a six-storey podium are being proposed at 1225 Dundas St. E. in Mississauga. Thirty-four townhouses are also proposed. City staff are recommending council approve an application to amend Mississauga’s official plan and zoning bylaw to permit two highrises that would bring hundreds of residential rental units to the Dixie neighbourhood. According to the city, the two 16-storey apartment buildings would be connected by a six-storey podium and contain a total of 553 residential units, along with ground-floor commercial space. The proposed development at 1225 Dundas St. , near Arena Road, also includes 34 four-storey back-to-back townhouses. 2-hectare (3-acre) site is owned by Stephen-Mitchell Realty Limited, Whitehorn Investments Limited, Lynrob Investments Limited, Richco Investments Limited and Tobdele Investments Limited, according to the city. items.title: 32 vehicles broken into in 30 minutes in Mississauga, man wanted
items.summary: Police are on the hunt for a man after more than 30 vehicles were broken into during a 30-minute span in Mississauga. m. m. in the area of Alpha Mills Road, Falconer Drive and Plainsman Road. Investigators said the suspect entered 32 vehicles by smashing windows or accessing those that had been left unlocked. Multiple valuables were stolen, though police did not specify what was taken. All of the vehicles were unoccupied at the time and none were stolen, police said. The suspect is described as a white man, approximately 30 years old with a medium build. He was reportedly wearing a jacket with the word “POLO” written on the back collar, joggers and two-tone shoes with white soles. He was also carrying a backpack. Police are asking anyone with information about the incidents or the suspect to contact 11 Division investigators at 905-453-2121, ext. 1133.

items.title: Police Release Suspect Photos After 32 Vehicle Break-Ins Hit Three Mississauga Streets
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Peel Regional Police have released photos of a suspect wanted in connection with at least 32 vehicle break-ins in Mississauga. The outlet reports the break-ins occurred on September 3 in the Alpha Mills Road, Falconer Drive and Plainsman Road areas. CityNews Toronto reports all of the vehicles were unoccupied at the time and that nothing was taken during the incidents. According to the outlet, the suspect is described as a white man approximately 30 years old with a medium build. CityNews Toronto reports he was last seen wearing a jacket with the word POLO written on the back collar, joggers, and two-toned shoes with a white sole, while carrying a backpack.

items.title: Square One, Celebration Square Among Mississauga Spots Staying Open Over Labour Day
items.summary: According to INsauga, several Mississauga businesses and attractions will remain open on Labour Day, September 7, even as most government offices and services close for the holiday. The outlet reports Square One Shopping Centre will be open, along with Walmart Supercentre, The Rec Room, The Food District, Whole Foods Square One and T&T Supermarket. INsauga reports Celebration Square and its fountain, select Rabba grocery stores and Beer Store locations, the city's YMCA health and fitness centre, and the Mississauga Chinese Centre will also be open, alongside movie theatres and many restaurants, cafes and bars. According to the outlet, Mississauga City Hall and Region of Peel offices will be closed for the day, along with banks, libraries and some community centres, and there will be no Canada Post pickup or delivery. INsauga reports garbage and recycling collection will be pushed back one day, MiWay will run on a regular Sunday schedule, and GO Transit will operate on a Saturday schedule.

items.title: MiWay Drops Route 110A as University Express Service Ramps Up for the School Year
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, MiWay is adjusting its bus schedule starting Tuesday, September 7, increasing service on some of its busiest corridors as students return to school. The outlet reports the changes include more frequent service on Route 110 University Express, which connects downtown Mississauga, the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, the Erin Mills community and Clarkson GO Station. Mississauga.com reports MiWay will discontinue its Route 110A University Express as part of the increased service on the main route. According to the outlet, two other routes will see reduced service due to lower ridership. Mississauga.com reports the schedule changes are also timed to resume regular school-day bus runs alongside the start of the new academic year.

items.title: GO Trains Diverted Around Port Credit After Saturday Night Lakeshore West Incident
items.summary: According to CP24, a person was struck by a GO train in Mississauga on Saturday night, prompting a shutdown of part of the Lakeshore West line. The outlet reports the circumstances surrounding the incident were not immediately known. CP24 reports the incident caused significant delays, with no train service between Port Credit and Exhibition stations. According to the outlet, GO Transit ran express buses between Port Credit and Kipling GO stations to help riders get around the closure. CP24 reports two train trips on the Lakeshore East line were also cancelled as a result of the incident.

items.title: Mississauga Accounts for Most of Peel's 300 Reported Vehicle Thefts Over Past Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows 300 vehicles were reported stolen across Mississauga and Brampton between August 5 and September 5, with more than half taken from Mississauga owners. The outlet reports 178 of those thefts occurred in Mississauga, 118 in Brampton, and the remaining four were not assigned a location on the force's crime map. INsauga reports the map identified hot spots including Toronto Pearson International Airport and the Square One shopping centre in Mississauga, along with the area of Bovaird Drive and Highway 410 in Brampton. According to the outlet, Brampton saw more violent crime over the same period, with 190 of a combined 320 reported assaults, or more than 59 per cent, occurring there compared with 127 in Mississauga. INsauga reports the data also showed 24 combined robberies across both cities, with six reported in Mississauga and 18 in Brampton.
